To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the vast majority of cases tumor‐infiltration of axillary lymph nodes by lymphoreticular cells is characterized by a predominance of macrophages, and that T‐lymphocyte subpopulations are present in a relatively low proportion.
tumor‐infiltrated lymph nodes show an accumulation of tumor‐inflitrating lymphoreticular infiltrate in the stroma, and that the tumor‐infltrating cells are mainly macrophages.
in axillary lymph nodes with metastatic deposits from breast cancer, the predominant lymphoreticular cells in the stromal areas are macrophages and helper T‐lymphocites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of lymphoreticular cells infiltrating axillary lymph node deposits in invasive ductal carcinomata of the breast and their frequency distribution.
the characterization and frequency distribution of tumor‐inflitrating lymphoreticular infiltrations in axillary lymph nodes of patients with breast carcinoma.
a quantitative analysis of the frequency of tumor‐invasive lymphoreticular cells in axillary lymph nodes metastatic for invasive ductal carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lymphoreticular cell infiltrate of the axillary lymph node is not a major factor in the defense against the metastasizing breast carcinoma.
the tumor‐inflitrating lymphoreticular cell population in axillary lymph nodes is dominated by macrophages.

the tumor‐inflitrating lymphoreticular infiltrate in axillary lymph nodes of invasive ductal carcinomata of the breast is predominantly composed of monocytes/macrophage‐like cells and CD4+ lymphocytic cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the majority of tumor‐associated lymphoreticular cells in the axillary lymph nodes of invasive ductal carcinomata of the breast are macrophages, which are probably involved in a variety of processes such as tumor‐associated antigen presentation, tumor‐associated antigen processing, and the release of tumor‐associated antigen‐binding antibodies.
the lymphoreticular infiltration is predominantly of a reactive nature.

the lymphoreticular cells infiltrating the axillary lymph nodes of breast carcinoma patients do not represent a highly differentiated and well‐coordinated host response to the tumor, but rather a heterogeneous mixture of lymphoreticular cells of various origins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lymphoreticular cell infiltrates are not a uniform population but are composed of various types of cells with different functional properties.
the frequency distribution of lymphocytes in axillary lymph nodes with metastatic deposits from invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast is not uniform, but varies greatly.

, in most cases of axillary lymph node involvement by ductal carcinoma of no special type, the metastases are not infiltrated by a high number of tumor‐specific lymphocytes, but rather by a high number (mostly monocytes/macrophage) of cells that are nonspecifically reactive to the tumor and are therefore not suitable for a specific immunotherapeutic approach.
